title: Cluster health: node & capacity
description: Single-node k8s01 at a glance: is the node healthy, how much CPU/memory/disk/network headroom is left, are pods running, restarting, OOM-killed or stuck? Built from the kubernetes-mixin and node-exporter-mixin recording rules and alert formulas (sources in each panel description). Curated companion of the official kube-prometheus-stack dashboards (Node Exporter / Nodes, Kubernetes / Compute Resources / *).

options.content:
**What this is.** The whole cluster is one machine, `k8s01` (8 CPU, 32 GB RAM, one ~220 GB SSD, NIC `enp3s0`).
If the node is sick, everything is sick, so this page answers: *is the node OK, how much room is left, and which pods are in trouble?*

**Healthy looks like:** top row all green (Ready, no pressure, schedulable, no firing alerts, no pending or crash-looping pods);
CPU and memory below ~80 %; root filesystem below 85 % and the *predicted free in 24 h* stat positive; no OOM kills; restarts flat.

**When something is red:**
- *Node pressure / NotReady* - the kubelet is evicting or the node is out of a resource: check the Memory and Disk rows, then `kubectl --context k8s01 describe node k8s01`.
- *Root filesystem* - **every PersistentVolume here is a directory on `/`** (local-path-provisioner, `/opt/local-path-provisioner`), together with container images, logs and emptyDirs. When `/` fills, all databases and Prometheus/Loki stop writing at once. Free space: `crictl rmi --prune`, Loki/Prometheus retention, old PVCs.
- *OOM kills / restarts* - find the pod in the tables of the *Pods & workloads* row, compare its memory with its limit (Kubernetes / Compute Resources / Pod).
- *Pending pods* - see the Warning events panel (FailedScheduling) and the *Control plane* dashboard (scheduler row).

**Expected here:** CPU requests can exceed 100 % only if requests outgrow 8 cores; there are no CPU limits by design, so CPU throttling panels elsewhere are empty.
PVC sizes are *not* enforced by local-path (it is a directory, not a quota): the PVC panel shows promises, the real limit is the root filesystem.

Formulas: [node-exporter mixin](https://github.com/prometheus/node_exporter/tree/master/docs/node-mixin), [kubernetes-mixin](https://github.com/kubernetes-monitoring/kubernetes-mixin). Annotations: firing alerts (red), container restarts (orange), kernel OOM kills (purple), node reboots (blue).

panels.title: Node Ready
panels.description:
Node condition Ready reported by the kubelet (kube-state-metrics `kube_node_status_condition`).
NOT READY means the kubelet stopped reporting or the container runtime/network is broken: nothing new can start.
Source: kubernetes-mixin alert KubeNodeNotReady (https://github.com/kubernetes-monitoring/kubernetes-mixin/tree/master/alerts/kubelet.libsonnet).

panels.title: Node pressure
panels.description:
Number of pressure conditions (MemoryPressure, DiskPressure, PIDPressure) that are true.
0 is healthy. Any pressure means the kubelet is about to evict pods (or already does) to protect the node.
Source: kubernetes-mixin alert KubeNodePressure (https://github.com/kubernetes-monitoring/kubernetes-mixin/tree/master/alerts/kubelet.libsonnet).

panels.title: Schedulable
panels.description:
Whether the node accepts new pods (`kube_node_spec_unschedulable`, https://github.com/kubernetes/kube-state-metrics/tree/main/docs/metrics/cluster/node-metrics.md).
CORDONED on a single node means no new pod can be scheduled anywhere: someone ran `kubectl cordon/drain` (maintenance)
and forgot to `uncordon`.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description:
Time since the node booted (`time() - node_boot_time_seconds`). A small value you did not expect
means an unplanned reboot (power, kernel panic, watchdog). Reboots also appear as blue annotations.

panels.title: Firing alerts
panels.description:
Alerts currently firing with severity warning or critical (Prometheus `ALERTS`).
Watchdog/InfoInhibitor (severity none) and info alerts are excluded. Details: Alertmanager UI or the red annotations.

panels.title: Pod slots used
panels.description:
Running pods divided by the node pod capacity (110 by kubelet default).
At 100 % the kubelet refuses new pods even with free CPU/memory. Red at 95 % = kubernetes-mixin alert KubeletTooManyPods
(https://github.com/kubernetes-monitoring/kubernetes-mixin/tree/master/alerts/kubelet.libsonnet).

panels.title: Pending pods
panels.description:
Pods in phase Pending (`kube_pod_status_phase`, https://github.com/kubernetes/kube-state-metrics/tree/main/docs/metrics/workload/pod-metrics.md): not
scheduled yet, or scheduled but still pulling images / waiting for a volume. A few seconds is normal during rollouts; a
pod Pending for more than 15 min fires KubePodNotReady. Look at FailedScheduling in the events panel below.

panels.title: CrashLoopBackOff
panels.description:
Containers waiting in CrashLoopBackOff (kube-state-metrics
`kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason`): they start, die, and the kubelet waits longer and longer before retrying.
Source: kubernetes-mixin alert KubePodCrashLooping (https://github.com/kubernetes-monitoring/kubernetes-mixin/tree/master/alerts/apps_alerts.libsonnet). Find them in the
*Containers waiting* table and read their logs (`kubectl logs --previous`).

panels.title: CPU utilisation
panels.description:
Share of the 8 CPUs busy (not idle/iowait/steal) over 5 min. Recording rule
`instance:node_cpu_utilisation:rate5m` from the node-exporter mixin (https://github.com/prometheus/node_exporter/tree/master/docs/node-mixin/rules/rules.libsonnet).
Red at 90 % = node-mixin alert NodeCPUHighUsage. Sustained high CPU makes every app slower; see the per-namespace panel.

panels.title: Load per CPU
panels.description:
1-minute load average divided by the number of CPUs (`instance:node_load1_per_cpu:ratio`,
node-exporter mixin). Above 1 = more runnable/IO-blocked tasks than CPUs. Red at 2 = node-mixin alert NodeSystemSaturation
(https://github.com/prometheus/node_exporter/tree/master/docs/node-mixin/alerts/alerts.libsonnet).

panels.title: CPU requests vs allocatable
panels.description:
Sum of CPU requests of all pods divided by the node's allocatable CPU.
Recording rule `namespace_cpu:kube_pod_container_resource_requests:sum` (kubernetes-mixin, https://github.com/kubernetes-monitoring/kubernetes-mixin/tree/master/rules/apps.libsonnet);
same ratio as the "CPU Requests Commitment" stat of Kubernetes / Compute Resources / Cluster. Above 100 % new pods with
CPU requests stay Pending (Insufficient cpu) = kubernetes-mixin alert KubeCPUOvercommit for a single node.
It is a reservation, not usage.

panels.title: CPU pressure (PSI)
panels.description:
Share of time at least one runnable task waited for a CPU (Linux Pressure Stall
Information "some", `rate(node_pressure_cpu_waiting_seconds_total)`; see https://docs.kernel.org/accounting/psi.html). Unlike utilisation, it measures
*waiting*: 0-5 % is fine, tens of percent means the node is CPU-starved and latency rises. No upstream alert threshold
exists, so no colour.

panels.title: CPU cores
panels.description:
Allocatable CPU cores of the node (kube-state-metrics `kube_node_status_allocatable`). The
reference for the per-namespace usage panel.

panels.title: CPU throttling
panels.description:
Not shown on purpose: no workload sets CPU limits in this lab (design choice), so CFS
throttling cannot happen and kps panels "CPU Throttling"/"CPU Quota" stay empty. This stat counts containers that do
have a CPU limit, so you notice if one appears.

panels.title: CPU usage by namespace
panels.description:
CPU cores used per namespace, stacked; dashed line = allocatable cores.
Recording rule `node_namespace_pod_container:container_cpu_usage_seconds_total:sum_rate5m` (kubernetes-mixin), same
query as "CPU Usage" in Kubernetes / Compute Resources / Cluster (https://github.com/prometheus-community/helm-charts/tree/kube-prometheus-stack-93.3.0/charts/kube-prometheus-stack/templates/grafana/dashboards-1.14/k8s-resources-cluster.yaml).
Tells you *who* is using the CPU when utilisation is high.

panels.title: CPU saturation over time
panels.description:
Utilisation (busy share), load per CPU and CPU PSI over time. Utilisation near 100 %
with PSI rising = real contention. Load per CPU above 2 for 15 min fires NodeSystemSaturation (node-exporter mixin,
https://github.com/prometheus/node_exporter/tree/master/docs/node-mixin).

panels.title: Memory utilisation
panels.description:
Share of RAM not available for new allocations: 1 - MemAvailable/MemTotal
(`instance:node_memory_utilisation:ratio`, node-exporter mixin https://github.com/prometheus/node_exporter/tree/master/docs/node-mixin/rules/rules.libsonnet). Page cache counts as
available. Red at 90 % = node-mixin alert NodeMemoryHighUtilization. There is no swap on this node: when memory runs out
the kubelet evicts pods and the kernel OOM-kills processes.

panels.title: Memory requests vs allocatable
panels.description:
Sum of memory requests divided by allocatable memory
(`namespace_memory:kube_pod_container_resource_requests:sum`, kubernetes-mixin https://github.com/kubernetes-monitoring/kubernetes-mixin/tree/master/rules/apps.libsonnet; "Memory
Requests Commitment" in Kubernetes / Compute Resources / Cluster). Above 100 % new pods stay Pending
(KubeMemoryOvercommit).

panels.title: Memory pressure (PSI)
panels.description:
Share of time at least one task stalled waiting for memory (reclaim, refaults),
`rate(node_pressure_memory_waiting_seconds_total)`, see https://docs.kernel.org/accounting/psi.html. Should be ~0 %. A few percent means the kernel is
fighting for memory before the OOM killer acts. No upstream threshold, no colour.

panels.title: Major page faults
panels.description:
Major page faults per second (`instance:node_vmstat_pgmajfault:rate5m`, node-exporter
mixin): pages read back from disk because memory was reclaimed. Red at 500/s = node-mixin alert
NodeMemoryMajorPagesFaults (thrashing).

panels.title: Kernel OOM kills (24h)
panels.description:
Processes killed by the Linux OOM killer in the last 24 h (`node_vmstat_oom_kill`
counter from /proc/vmstat). Includes containers hitting their memory limit (cgroup OOM) and node-wide OOM. Any value
> 0: find the victim in the *OOM-killed containers* table.

panels.title: Memory total
panels.description: Physical memory of the node (node_memory_MemTotal_bytes).

panels.title: Memory usage by namespace (working set)
panels.description:
Working-set memory per namespace, stacked; dashed line = allocatable.
Working set is what the kubelet uses for evictions and what memory limits are checked against. Recording rule
`node_namespace_pod_container:container_memory_working_set_bytes` (kubernetes-mixin https://github.com/kubernetes-monitoring/kubernetes-mixin/tree/master/rules/apps.libsonnet).

panels.title: Node memory breakdown
Disk & storage (root filesystem holds every PersistentVolume)
Root filesystem used
panels.description:
Used share of `/` (ext4 on /dev/sda2). This one filesystem holds the OS, container
images and logs, emptyDirs **and every PersistentVolume** (local-path, /opt/local-path-provisioner). Thresholds follow
the node-exporter mixin filesystem alerts (https://github.com/prometheus/node_exporter/tree/master/docs/node-mixin/alerts/alerts.libsonnet): 85 % used (15 % free) = NodeFilesystemSpaceFillingUp
warning when also predicted full within 24 h; 95 % / 97 % = NodeFilesystemAlmostOutOfSpace warning / critical. The kubelet
also starts evicting pods (DiskPressure) when free space drops under 10 % by default.

panels.title: Root free
panels.description: Free bytes on `/` available to non-root users (node_filesystem_avail_bytes).

panels.title: Predicted free in 24h
panels.description:
Linear extrapolation of the free space 24 h ahead from the last 6 h trend:
`predict_linear(node_filesystem_avail_bytes[6h], 24h)` - the exact projection used by the node-mixin alert
NodeFilesystemSpaceFillingUp (https://github.com/prometheus/node_exporter/tree/master/docs/node-mixin/alerts/alerts.libsonnet). Negative (red) = at the current rate the disk fills within a day.

panels.title: Inodes used
panels.description:
Used share of inodes on `/` (1 - files_free/files). Many tiny files (images, logs) can
exhaust inodes before bytes. Same thresholds as the node-mixin NodeFilesystemFilesFillingUp/AlmostOutOfFiles alerts
(95 % / 97 % used).

panels.title: PVC requests vs disk
panels.description:
Sum of the storage requested by all PVCs divided by the size of `/`
(kube-state-metrics `kube_persistentvolumeclaim_resource_requests_storage_bytes`, https://github.com/kubernetes/kube-state-metrics/tree/main/docs/metrics/storage/persistentvolumeclaim-metrics.md).
local-path does **not** enforce PVC sizes (a PV is just a directory), so this is how much space has been *promised*;
above 100 % the promises cannot all be kept. Derived ratio, no upstream threshold.

panels.title: Root filesystem free + 24h projection
panels.description:
Free bytes on `/` and the 24 h projection used by
NodeFilesystemSpaceFillingUp (node-exporter mixin). When the dashed projection reaches 0 the warning fires
(if also < 15 % free). Sudden drops = image pulls, a database bulk load, Prometheus/Loki compaction.

panels.title: Disk I/O utilisation and saturation
panels.description:
Utilisation = share of time the disk was busy
(`instance_device:node_disk_io_time_seconds:rate5m`); saturation = average I/O queue depth
(`instance_device:node_disk_io_time_weighted_seconds:rate5m`), both node-exporter mixin recording rules. Queue above 10
for 30 min = node-mixin alert NodeDiskIOSaturation. etcd is very sensitive to slow disk: check etcd fsync in the
Control plane dashboard when this is high.

panels.title: Disk throughput and I/O pressure
panels.description:
Bytes read/written per second on the physical disk (node-exporter mixin
"Disk I/O" panel: rate of node_disk_read_bytes_total / node_disk_written_bytes_total) and I/O PSI (share of time at least
one task stalled on I/O, https://docs.kernel.org/accounting/psi.html, right axis).

panels.title: Top disk writers (pods)
panels.description:
Top 10 pods by bytes written per second (cAdvisor
`container_fs_writes_bytes_total`, as in the "Storage IO" panels of Kubernetes / Compute Resources / Namespace
(https://github.com/prometheus-community/helm-charts/tree/kube-prometheus-stack-93.3.0/charts/kube-prometheus-stack/templates/grafana/dashboards-1.14/k8s-resources-namespace.yaml)). Answers "who is wearing the SSD / filling the disk". etcd, Loki and
Prometheus are expected at the top.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (namespace, pod) (rate(container_fs_writes_bytes_total{job="kubelet", metrics_path="/metrics/cadvisor", container!=""}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: PersistentVolumeClaims (requested size, not usage)
panels.description:
Every PVC with its requested size, StorageClass and
PV. kubelet reports **no per-volume usage** for these PVs: for `local` PVs it reports the statfs of the whole root
filesystem (capacity = disk size), for `hostPath` PVs nothing at all - so the kps "Persistent Volumes" dashboard and the
KubePersistentVolumeFillingUp alert effectively watch `/`, not each PVC. Data: kube-state-metrics
`kube_persistentvolumeclaim_resource_requests_storage_bytes` x `kube_persistentvolumeclaim_info`
(https://github.com/kubernetes/kube-state-metrics/tree/main/docs/metrics/storage/persistentvolumeclaim-metrics.md).

targets.expr: max by (namespace, persistentvolumeclaim, storageclass, volumename) (kube_persistentvolumeclaim_resource_requests_storage_bytes{job="kube-state-metrics"} * on (namespace, persistentvolumeclaim) group_left (storageclass, volumename) kube_persistentvolumeclaim_info{job="kube-state-metrics"})

panels.title: NIC throughput
panels.description:
Bytes per second received/transmitted on the physical NIC (enp3s0; matched as en*/eth*/wl*).
Pod-to-pod traffic stays on cali* veths and does not show here. Same counters as the node-exporter mixin "Network
Traffic" panel (https://github.com/prometheus/node_exporter/tree/master/docs/node-mixin).

panels.title: NIC errors and drops
panels.description:
Receive/transmit errors and dropped packets per second on the physical NIC. Should be 0.
Persistent errors = cable/driver problem (node-mixin alerts NodeNetworkReceiveErrs/TransmitErrs, https://github.com/prometheus/node_exporter/tree/master/docs/node-mixin/alerts/alerts.libsonnet).

panels.title: Conntrack table used
panels.description:
Connection-tracking entries / limit. Every Service connection (kube-proxy iptables,
Calico) uses an entry; when the table is full new connections are dropped. Red at 75 % = node-mixin alert
NodeHighNumberConntrackEntriesUsed (https://github.com/prometheus/node_exporter/tree/master/docs/node-mixin/alerts/alerts.libsonnet).

panels.title: Pods by phase
panels.description:
Number of pods per phase (kube-state-metrics `kube_pod_status_phase`). Running should be flat;
Pending spikes during rollouts are fine; Failed pods are usually finished Jobs kept for their logs.

panels.title: Container restarts by namespace
panels.description:
Container restarts per namespace in each interval
(`increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total)`, kube-state-metrics). A namespace that restarts continuously is
crash-looping (KubePodCrashLooping); a single bar after a deploy or node reboot is normal.

panels.title: Containers restarted (1h)
panels.description: Distinct containers that restarted at least once in the last hour.

panels.title: Failed Jobs
panels.description:
Jobs with failed pods (kube-state-metrics `kube_job_status_failed` > 0), the condition of
kubernetes-mixin alert KubeJobFailed (https://github.com/kubernetes-monitoring/kubernetes-mixin/tree/master/alerts/apps_alerts.libsonnet). Backups, sweepers and CronJobs live here.

panels.title: Pods not healthy
panels.description:
Pods Pending/Unknown/Failed, or Running but not Ready - the two conditions of the
kubernetes-mixin alert KubePodNotReady (https://github.com/kubernetes-monitoring/kubernetes-mixin/tree/master/alerts/apps_alerts.libsonnet). Empty = all good. Failed pods of finished
Jobs also appear until the Job is cleaned up.

targets.expr: label_replace(max by (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_status_ready{job="kube-state-metrics", condition="false"} == 1) and on (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_status_phase{job="kube-state-metrics", phase="Running"} == 1), "phase", "Running, not Ready", "", "")

panels.title: Containers waiting
panels.description:
Containers that are not running and why (CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff,
CreateContainerConfigError, ...) from kube-state-metrics `kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason`. Source:
KubeContainerWaiting / KubePodCrashLooping alerts (https://github.com/kubernetes-monitoring/kubernetes-mixin/tree/master/alerts/apps_alerts.libsonnet). Empty = all good.

panels.title: OOM-killed containers
panels.description:
Containers whose last termination was OOMKilled (kube-state-metrics
`kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason`, current state) and pods with cgroup OOM events in the last 24 h
(cAdvisor `container_oom_events_total`). Fix: raise the memory limit or fix the leak; compare usage with the limit in
Kubernetes / Compute Resources / Pod.

targets.expr: label_replace(max by (namespace, pod, container) (kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason{job="kube-state-metrics", reason="OOMKilled"}) == 1, "source", "last termination OOMKilled", "", "")
label_replace(sum by (namespace, pod) (increase(container_oom_events_total{job="kubelet", metrics_path="/metrics/cadvisor"}[24h])) > 0, "source", "cgroup OOM events (24h)", "", "")

panels.title: Most restarted containers (24h)
panels.description:
Top 15 containers by restarts over the last 24 h
(`increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total[24h])`).

panels.title: Kubernetes Warning events
panels.description:
Warning events from the Kubernetes API (FailedScheduling, BackOff, Unhealthy,
FailedMount, Evicted, OOMKilling, ProvisioningFailed...) collected by the OpenTelemetry k8sobjects receiver into Loki
(`service_name="k8s-events"`). Kyverno PolicyViolation events are filtered out (audit noise, see the Security folder).
This is usually the fastest way to learn *why* a pod is Pending or restarting.

panels.title: Kubelet
panels.description: Prometheus can scrape the kubelet /metrics endpoint (KubeletDown alert when absent).

panels.title: PLEG relist p99
panels.description:
99th percentile duration of the kubelet's Pod Lifecycle Event Generator relist (how long
the kubelet needs to see container state changes from containerd). Recording rule
`node_quantile:kubelet_pleg_relist_duration_seconds:histogram_quantile` (kubernetes-mixin). Red at 10 s = alert
KubeletPlegDurationHigh (https://github.com/kubernetes-monitoring/kubernetes-mixin/tree/master/alerts/kubelet.libsonnet); a slow PLEG precedes the node going NotReady.

panels.title: Pod worker p99
panels.description:
99th percentile time the kubelet pod worker spends syncing a pod
(`kubelet_pod_worker_duration_seconds`), formula of alert KubeletPodStartUpLatencyHigh (red at 60 s,
https://github.com/kubernetes-monitoring/kubernetes-mixin/tree/master/alerts/kubelet.libsonnet). High = slow image pulls, volume mounts or a struggling container runtime.

panels.title: Container runtime operation errors
panels.description:
Errors per second of kubelet -> containerd (CRI) operations by type
(`kubelet_runtime_operations_errors_total`), as in the "Operation Error Rate" panel of Kubernetes / Kubelet
(https://github.com/prometheus-community/helm-charts/tree/kube-prometheus-stack-93.3.0/charts/kube-prometheus-stack/templates/grafana/dashboards-1.14/kubelet.yaml). Occasional errors during pod deletion are normal; a steady rate means containerd trouble.

panels.title: Temperatures
panels.description:
Hardware sensor temperatures from hwmon (node_hwmon_temp_celsius) per chip/sensor. A mini PC in
a closet throttles its CPU when hot. The kernel's own critical limit per sensor (node_hwmon_temp_crit_celsius) is the
reference: stay well below it. Sensor names depend on the board (coretemp = CPU package/cores, nvme = SSD).

panels.title: Clock offset
panels.description:
Offset of the system clock from NTP as seen by the kernel (node_timex_offset_seconds). TLS,
etcd leases and token validation need a correct clock. Red line at 50 ms = node-mixin alert NodeClockSkewDetected; the
NodeClockNotSynchronising alert uses node_timex_sync_status (https://github.com/prometheus/node_exporter/tree/master/docs/node-mixin/alerts/alerts.libsonnet).
